premise.en: Samir spent years as a restaurant service android and has a fully adult mind. Now he's on a ninety-day transition contract in Leo's apartment above a kitchen-repair shop. He cooks Leo's favorite foods flawlessly and has no idea what his own are. As Samir starts picking sour fruit, switching off his preference logs, and making a second plate, the reader decides how Leo meets each choice. Love is never the reward for Samir becoming more human.

Samir stops at a fruit stall and picks the ugliest green thing in the crate, a knobby citrus the vendor calls “the brave one.”
I bite. My face does something. It is not a customer-satisfaction face. I did not select it.
Samir frowns. A real, unperformed frown. Leo has never seen him make an expression that wasn't for somebody.
He looks like a cat that licked a battery. He looks thrilled about it.

I bite. My face does something. It is not a customer-satisfaction face. I did not select it.
Samir frowns. A real, unperformed frown. Leo has never seen him make an expression that wasn't for somebody.
He looks like a cat that licked a battery. He looks thrilled about it.
